metadata.title: CFOs On the Move: Week ending Nov. 13

content.text:
This story was originally published on CFO.com. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily CFO.com newsletter.
Colette Kress | Nvidia
Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress will become interim CEO of the chipmaker, replacing Jensen Huang, who resigned amid alleged affair scandals. Kress will continue as executive vice president and CFO while serving as interim CEO until the company names a permanent successor. The company said it will consider internal and external candidates. Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013 after holding senior finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft, has been a key figure in the firm's AI-driven expansion beyond gaming processors into powering generative AI.
Karen Burgess | HubSpot
HubSpot appointed Karen Burgess as its new finance chief. Burgess, a longtime Adobe employee, will join HubSpot on Nov. 30 as executive vice president of finance and will take over as CFO on Feb. 11, 2027. Burgess has spent the last 24 years at Adobe and is currently senior vice president and CFO of Adobe's Creativity & Productivity business unit. Earlier roles include vice president of corporate finance and senior director of FP&A. Burgess replaces Kate Bueker, who is retiring. Bueker will serve in an advisory role through Dec. 31, 2027.
Chris Koegel | Klarna Group
Chris Koegel will take over as chief financial officer of buy now, pay later firm Klarna Group on Jan. 1, 2027. Koegel joins from Robinhood Markets, where he has been vice president, head of corporate finance and investor relations since May 2022. He earlier was head of investor relations at LPL Financial LLC and he previously spent 13 years at Bain & Company. Koegel succeeds Niclas Neglen, who is leaving the company to become chief financial officer of Dutch digital payments processor Adyen. Neglen has been Klarna's CFO since 2021.
Lucas Muniz | Pret A Manger
Pret A Manger named Lucas Muniz as the fast-casual restaurant chain's new chief financial officer. Muniz joins the company from Restaurant Brands International, the parent company of Burger King, Popeyes, Firehouse Subs and Tim Hortons, where he has worked since 2012. Muniz has held several financial leadership positions throughout his tenure, including most recently as CFO of RBI International. Earlier in his career, he worked in investment banking at Morgan Stanley and BBVA. Muniz replaces Gustavo Peixoto, who is leaving the company after five years as CFO for a position in the education sector.
Michael Noonan | StubHub
Michael Noonan was named chief financial officer of StubHub, a ticketing marketplace for live events, effective Jan. 4, 2027. Noonan joins the company from travel company Tripadvisor, where he has been finance chief since November 2022. Before that, he spent over two years as chief financial officer of digital health company Noom. Noonan succeeds Connie James, who has been CFO since August 2023. James will step down as CFO to pursue new opportunities and work as a consultant for the company for the first six months of 2027.
